market_context: U.S. equities are staging a massive broad-based relief rally following last week's post-election and tech sell-off, with the S&P 500 up over 2.5% and the VIX tumbling more than 23% below 20. Communication services, consumer discretionary, and broader semiconductors (e.g., AMD, AMAT) are surging, while Nvidia trades down 5% as it decouples due to news regarding CEO Jensen Huang and foreign intelligence scrutiny. With strong closing market-on-close demand anticipated across broad indexes, equity benchmarks are poised to finish near session highs.

predictions.reasoning: The broad market is maintaining relentless upside momentum into the final half hour, supported by all 11 S&P 500 sectors trading higher and safe-haven volatility collapsing. Institutional Market-On-Close buy imbalances in a trend-day rally typically keep price action buoyant near the top of the session range ($755.42). With Treasury yields stabilizing and oil declining, macro headwinds are muted heading into the 4:00 PM ET bell.

Despite sharp weakness in Nvidia, the broader semiconductor sector and mega-cap tech peers like META and MSFT are experiencing aggressive dip-buying, pushing QQQ up over 3.7%. Strong closing program buying on high-beta tech is expected to push the ETF closer to its session peak of $681.70 into the bell. Upward momentum across communications and tech constituents remains dominant in late afternoon trading.

Nvidia is facing distinct idiosyncratic selling pressure following weekend reports regarding Jensen Huang and subsequent congressional inquiry announcements. Although shares bounced from the intraday low of $170.24, traders and funds are likely to de-risk and trim long exposure into the close rather than hold overnight event risk. This overhang should keep NVDA soft into the 4:00 PM close relative to its late-afternoon bounce.

Meta is among the primary beneficiaries of rotation back into big-tech platform leaders, advancing 6% and hovering right at its session high of $647.25. Communication services continue to lead sector-level performance across Wall Street. Sustained late-day institutional inflows should support a strong finish right against session highs at the closing print.
